relations.rationale: Traveling the farthest distance is unrelated to finishing order between Zeno and Vik.
Distance traveled to compete has no bearing on Vik finishing ahead of Pia.
Traveling far to compete has no logical connection to Pia and Tess leaving together afterward.
Tess taking photographs has no bearing on when Alma arrived.
Taking photographs is unrelated to height comparisons.
Taking photographs has no bearing on race finishing order.
Being tallest is unrelated to finishing position in the race.
Zeno being tallest of the group supports the idea that Tess, a group member, is shorter than others including possibly Pia.
Zeno's height has no connection to the difficulty of the final descent.
Zeno stretching near the registration tent during warm-up doesn't establish who arrived earliest, so it neither confirms nor denies Alma's early arrival.
The course winding through villages before looping back doesn't specify difficulty of the final descent, though it sets up the route including the descent.
Spectators lining the road has no bearing on relative ages of Vik and Tess.
Spectators lining roads is unrelated to training rigor comparisons.
Spectators with flags and snacks has no bearing on race finishing order.
Spectators lining the roads during the race is unrelated to Alma's post-race chatting near the finish.
Spectators at this race have no bearing on scheduling of a future event.
Pia finishing ahead of Zeno has no bearing on age comparison between Vik and Alma.
Pia finishing ahead of Zeno is independent of Zeno's finish relative to Vik.

If Pia finished ahead of Zeno, and Zeno likely finished ahead of others depending on order, this alone doesn't determine whether Vik finished ahead of Pia, making it largely unrelated, though it constrains possible orderings.
Alma arriving earliest of everyone supports the idea that she arrived long before sunrise, consistent with an especially early arrival.
